title: Fix all bugs found by the hq-gbl regression suite (15 bugs + contract/doc drift)
description:
WHY: The hq-gbl regression suite (merged to main at aa106e9) surfaced 15 real product bugs plus contract/doc-drift items, each already pinned by a strict xfail (xfail(strict=True) citing the bead id) in tests/regression or encoded as observed behavior in the unit matrices. This epic fixes them. Every fix self-verifies: removing/flipping the cited xfail (it XPASS-fails until the fix lands) and updating the unit-matrix CASES expectations from observed to desired behavior.

CONVENTIONS for every child bead:
- The bead description carries the root cause (file:line) and FIX guidance - follow it; if the fix diverges, say why in the report.
- Each fix MUST: (1) change the production code; (2) add/adjust unit tests asserting the emitted script/URL or returned contract (tests/unit/test_write_input_matrix.py / test_read_input_matrix.py CASES updated from observed to desired - the completeness checks and meta-lint must stay green); (3) flip/remove the strict xfail(s) named in the bead (tests/regression/*); (4) add a CHANGELOG.md entry under ## [Unreleased]; (5) update CLAUDE.md/README where the documented behavior changes.
- Live verification: unit suite green (PYTHONPATH=src, uv venv at /Users/ebowman/src/mcp-server-things-wt/.venv, baseline 2024 passed 1 skipped at epic start, grows as fixes land), then the affected tests/regression file(s) live (THINGS_MCP_LIVE_TESTS=1, foreground, never two live runs concurrently), throwaway objects prefixed 'hq-fix ' and trashed. The FULL live suite runs once in the final verification bead, not per-bead.
- Schema changes (new validation, minLength etc.) require regenerating tests/fixtures/tool_schema_snapshot.json (THINGS_MCP_UPDATE_SCHEMA_SNAPSHOT=1) and scripts/gen_manifest_tools.py --write if tool docs change.
- Dependencies below serialize beads that touch the same files (scheduling/helpers+strategies, todo_operations.py, move_operations.py, server.py read plumbing, tag paths) to avoid conflicting edits.

title: Bug: add_todo/update_todo when='anytime' lands in Someday via AppleScript list fallback
description:
Found by the hq-gbl regression seed oracle (hq-gbl.6) and independently confirmed live by the reviewer: add_todo(when='anytime') returns scheduling.method='list_fallback', date_set='Someday'; things.get -> start='Someday', start_date=None - identical to when='someday'. Root cause: src/things_mcp/scheduling/helpers.py:50-51 determine_target_list maps when_lower in ['someday','anytime'] both to 'Someday', reached via scheduling/strategies.py Strategy 4 _schedule_list_fallback (~line 213). Contradicts CLAUDE.md / server.py Field docs for when='anytime' (and the documented 'use when=anytime to unschedule' guidance on update_todo).
FIX: map 'anytime' to the Anytime list (AppleScript: move to list "Anytime" or set activation date to missing value + not someday - verify live which works); add unit tests asserting the emitted script for when='anytime' vs 'someday' on add_todo, update_todo, bulk_update_todos, add_project, update_project; then flip the two XFAILS entries in tests/regression/test_seed_oracle.py (they are strict, so they will XPASS-fail until removed). Verify live with a throwaway to-do (prefix 'hq-gbl-fix ') that start=='Anytime'. CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.
DONE: when='anytime' yields start='Anytime' live; unit tests on emitted script; seed-oracle xfails removed; suite green.

title: Comprehensive API regression suite (all 41 MCP tools, live + unit, self-cleaning)
description:
WHY: v1.7.0 fixed bugs that the unit suite could not see because it never exercised real inputs end-to-end. We want a regression suite that covers the ENTIRE API surface (41 MCP tools) across the full range of inputs the code accepts, so future changes cannot silently break any tool/parameter/value class.

DESIGN (two layers, both required):
1. Live regression suite tests/regression/ (opt-in: THINGS_MCP_LIVE_TESTS=1 AND Things 3 running, same gate as tests/live). Every call goes THROUGH THE MCP BOUNDARY: fastmcp Client(server.mcp) on a ThingsMCPServer built with a real AppleScriptManager - so pydantic schema validation and server.py validation are exercised, not just ThingsTools. A session sandbox fixture creates ONE throwaway area, ONE throwaway project (with a real heading seeded via add_project todos='##...'), and ONE throwaway tag, plus a deterministic seed set of to-dos covering every list/status/date class. Every created id is tracked; teardown trashes to-dos/projects, deletes the area and tag via AppleScript, then verifies via things.py that nothing tracked remains. A zero-collateral-writes guard snapshots modificationDate of every pre-existing item before the session and asserts none changed afterward. LIVE-WRITE SAFETY: never write into, move into, or modify any pre-existing project/area/heading/tag/to-do.
2. CI-runnable unit layers: a golden tool-schema snapshot (names, params, types, defaults, required) and a table-driven input-space matrix per tool (every param x value class -> expected error code / emitted AppleScript or URL), mock-backed.

Then: coverage measurement (branch coverage of src/things_mcp under unit+regression) that files targeted follow-up beads per under-covered module; docs/TESTING.md + Makefile target + release checklist wiring.

CONVENTIONS for every task: tests live under tests/regression/ (live) or tests/unit/ (mock); use the shared harness helpers from the harness bead (call_tool, sandbox, read_back_with_retry); assert on structured_content, never on prose text; every write test reads the result back (tool read and/or things.py) and asserts the actual state; every negative test asserts the structured error code per the documented read (lower_snake) / write (UPPER_SNAKE) contracts in CLAUDE.md. Run with: THINGS_MCP_LIVE_TESTS=1 pytest tests/regression -q. Use the uv venv at /Users/ebowman/src/mcp-server-things-wt/.venv (fastmcp 3.x) for all runs. Never print or commit the Things auth token (.things-auth at repo root).

title: Fix GH issues #9 and #10 and ship release v1.7.0
description:
Why: Two open GitHub issues, both verified still present in v1.6.2 on 2026-08-19.

GH #10 (URL/AppleScript escaping):
- Bug 1+2 (read path): get_todos(project_uuid=...) uses the AppleScript read path (tools_helpers/read_operations.py:158-160). services/applescript/queries.py:100,186 emits the `name` field raw (only notes/dates get §COMMA§ protection), so services/applescript/parser.py:158-160 splits titles at the first comma and :145-149/:200-207 strips literal double quotes. Every other read tool uses things.py and is unaffected.
- Bug 3 (write path): utils/applescript_utils.py:33-35 AppleScriptTemplates.escape_string replaces '\n'/'\r' with spaces, collapsing multi-line notes in add_todo/update_todo/add_project/update_project (scheduling/todo_operations.py:82,532,669,818). Areas unaffected (no notes). URL-scheme path (formatters.py:42, %0A) preserves newlines.

GH #9 (data quality + headings):
- tools_helpers/read_operations.py:568 things.anytime(), :611 things.someday(), :520 things.today(), :544 things.upcoming(), :498 things.inbox() are called with no type filter; things.py returns to-do + project + heading. Live DB: anytime 1175 = 1106 to-do + 39 project + 30 heading; someday 77 = 54 + 23 project; today 130 = 114 + 16 project. tools_helpers/helpers.py:114-148 convert_todo drops `type`, `heading`, `heading_title`, so callers cannot even filter client-side.
- add_todo(heading=...) is declared (server.py:387) but only honoured on the URL-scheme path, which is taken only when checklist_items is non-empty (scheduling/todo_operations.py:148-166); the AppleScript path silently drops it.
- No heading read tool. Things 3 AppleScript dictionary has NO heading class (sdef confirms zero matches); URL scheme `add`/`update` accept `heading`/`heading-id` (existing headings only); `add-project` can create headings via `##` lines in `to-dos`. Rename/delete/reorder headings is impossible via any public API - out of scope, to be stated in the issue reply.

High-level design:
1. Fix AppleScript read-path title corruption (placeholder-protect name for comma/quote/colon in queries.py, unescape in parser(s)).
2. Fix escape_string newline collapse (emit \n / \r escapes instead of spaces).
3. Type-filter the five list tools (to-do only by default; include_projects flag on today/upcoming/anytime/someday).
4. Expose type/heading/headingTitle on todo dicts (+ best-effort heading enrichment on the AppleScript get_todos path).
5. add_todo(heading=...) routes to URL scheme whenever heading is set; new get_project_headings tool; update_todo(heading=...) via URL-scheme update.
6. Bump to 1.7.0 (new tool + params => minor), CHANGELOG/README/CLAUDE.md/UPGRADING, manifest tools regen, release per CLAUDE.md Release Process, reply on + close #9/#10.

Constraints: 100% backward compatible; pytest tests/unit must pass after every bead; verify write/URL-scheme changes against real Things 3 (create a throwaway item, read it back via things.py, trash it).

Scope update 2026-08-19: the 14 post-sweep hardening beads (formerly epic hq-nxu) are reparented here per user decision - everything ships in v1.7.0. Release prep (hq-f0w.15) and the live smoke suite (hq-f0w.14) are gated on all of them.
close_reason: Epic complete: 58 beads closed across 4 goal runs; v1.7.0 released (PyPI + GitHub release + .mcpb), GH #9/#10 closed.

title: Harden generated uvx launch configs against x86_64 Python selection (.mcpb failed in Claude Desktop)
description: Real-world failure: user double-clicked mcp-server-things-1.6.1.mcpb; Claude Desktop's uvx resolved an x86_64 Python (miniconda visible in the app environment), cryptography==50.0.0 has no macOS x86_64 wheels, maturin source build failed (rustup target missing), server never started. Log: ~/Library/Logs/Claude/mcp-server-Things 3 MCP.log. Verified fix: 'uvx --python-preference only-managed --python 3.12 mcp-server-things@1.6.1 doctor' downloads/uses uv's managed arm64 CPython and passes all checks. Fix: (1) manifest.json server.mcp_config.args -> ['--python-preference','only-managed','--python','3.12','mcp-server-things']; (2) client_config.py build_server_config uvx variant emits the same hardened args (affects config --client ... output and --write); update tests asserting the old args and the README/UPGRADING snippets that show the generated JSON; (3) keep plain 'uvx mcp-server-things' in prose examples with the existing troubleshooting note. Trade-off: first launch downloads a managed CPython (~30-60s one-time).
acceptance_criteria: manifest and config CLI emit hardened uvx args; tests updated; live uvx run with only-managed passes doctor; .mcpb rebuilt for 1.6.2.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS incl. live PATH-pollution test; committed on fix/hq-mcpb

title: Install experience: match or beat hald/things-mcp (uvx-first, one-click, doctor, smooth upgrade)
description:
WHY: hald/things-mcp installs with one command (uvx things-mcp), one click (.mcpb), and a 3-line prereq list; ours currently offers four install options, verbose env config, a published wheel whose console script only works in editable installs (fixed on epic/hq-5wb, unreleased), and no single 'is it working?' step. Both servers read Things' SQLite via things.py, so hald's documented TCC failure (reads fail with 'unable to open database file' when Claude Desktop launches the server via its disclaimer helper; writes still work) applies to us and is undocumented here.
DESIGN: (1) uvx-first install story with .mcpb one-click and a claude-code one-liner; pip/venv/source preserved under Advanced. (2) A 'doctor' subcommand that verifies Things, Automation permission, DB readability (TCC), uv on PATH, and prints fixes — an improvement over hald, who has none. (3) A 'config' subcommand that prints (or safely writes) the client config so users never hand-edit JSON paths. (4) HTTP transport for parity and as the TCC fix ladder. (5) An explicit upgrade guide so existing venv/pip users keep working (things-mcp alias, python -m things_mcp) and can move to uvx when ready. (6) A PyPI release + .mcpb attach (human-executed) so uvx/.mcpb actually resolve.
CONSTRAINTS: no breaking changes for existing installs; Automation permission prompt is unavoidable (AppleScript writes) and must be documented, not hidden. Out of scope: bundling a full Python runtime in the .mcpb (uv-based bundle is more robust than relying on system python3).
BASE: build on epic/hq-k40 (which sits on epic/hq-5wb → origin/main v1.5.0).
close_reason: All children closed: parity/install epic complete; v1.6.0+v1.6.1 released and verified

title: Filter Someday-project tasks out of Today/Anytime/Upcoming (match Things UI)
description:
Why: things.py reports tasks inside a Someday project with their own start/anytime state, so get_today, get_anytime, get_upcoming (and get_todos activating-in-days variants) return items the Things UI hides. hald fixed this in v0.7.3 (src/things_mcp/server.py filter_someday_project_tasks + tests/test_someday_filtering.py) — reference that implementation.
Steps:
1. In src/things_mcp/tools_helpers/read_operations.py (or wherever get_today/get_anytime/get_upcoming build their lists), add a helper that loads the set of project UUIDs whose start == 'Someday' (things.projects(start='Someday')) once per call.
2. Drop any todo whose project (direct) OR whose heading's parent project is in that set from Today/Anytime/Upcoming/date-window results. Handle both 'project' and 'heading' membership — heading-parented todos do not carry the project UUID directly; resolve via the heading record.
3. get_someday must INCLUDE tasks belonging to Someday projects that things.py labels Anytime, and annotate them (e.g. an 'inherited_someday': true field or list label 'Someday (inherited from project)').
4. Edge cases: project missing/deleted → treat as not-Someday; todo with no project → keep; completed/canceled todos are out of scope for these views already.
5. Unit tests with mocked things.py data: task directly in Someday project, task under a heading in Someday project, task in Anytime project (control), standalone task (control). Cover today/anytime/upcoming/someday.
acceptance_criteria: get_today/get_anytime/get_upcoming exclude tasks in Someday projects (direct and via heading); get_someday includes them with an inherited marker; new unit tests pass; full pytest suite passes.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS; squash-merged to epic/hq-5wb

title: Diagnose & harden intermittent overnight cold-start MCP boot hang
description: Nightly llm-wiki sweep reports the things MCP server intermittently never completes the stdio handshake at overnight cold-start (60s connect timeout at 01:00Z on 2026-07-19/20; normal nights connect in 1.3-2.1s). Recurred May (hq-eww) and June (hq-h8v) in the consumer's tracker. Server-side stderr shows nothing, so the hang location is unknown. Code audit shows startup already avoids osascript (main.py:53-59 lazy probe fix) and _load_auth_token is file-only, so the cause is upstream of tool registration: interpreter/import stall, logging config, or module-level work. Design: (1) emit timestamped boot-phase markers to stderr from the first line of the entrypoint, (2) add a faulthandler-based startup watchdog that dumps all thread stacks to stderr if the server is not serving within a deadline, (3) audit the pre-handshake boot path for blocking I/O and file follow-ups, (4) release and advertise. OUT OF SCOPE: client-side mitigations (bump MCP_TIMEOUT in the sweep, gate connect-retry with backoff) live in llm-wiki's hq tracker, mirroring hq-0a3 for hermes.
close_reason: all steps complete

description:
Goal: leave the repo with a single clean main branch, no uncommitted changes, no stray files, no stale branches.

title: Final verification: full live regression suite green with zero unexpected xfails/xpasses; docs/CHANGELOG consolidation
description:
Runs LAST, after every fix bead in epic hq-cal.
1. grep tests/regression tests/unit for xfail markers citing fixed bead ids (hq-z5d hq-x9z hq-4gn hq-rmh hq-edj hq-cag hq-exe hq-r87 hq-9tm hq-exd hq-lsb hq-3bp) - all must be gone; any survivor means a fix bead was closed without flipping its xfail: reopen that bead, do not paper over.
2. Unit suite green (PYTHONPATH=src, uv venv). Full live regression suite (THINGS_MCP_LIVE_TESTS=1 pytest tests/regression -q, foreground, ~30 min): 0 failures, 0 unexpected xpasses; remaining xfails only for beads intentionally NOT fixed in this epic (list them in the report).
3. tests/live smoke suite green (THINGS_MCP_LIVE_TESTS=1 pytest tests/live -q).
4. CHANGELOG.md: consolidate the Unreleased entries added by the fix beads into coherent Fixed/Changed sections (no version bump - release is a separate decision).
5. CLAUDE.md/docs sweep: grep for statements the fixes invalidated (anytime/Someday, summary field set, requested_mode, destination table, checklist cap, tag policy env) - all updated by their beads; fix any stragglers.
DONE: all three suites green with the expected xfail set; CHANGELOG coherent; no doc contradictions; cleanup sweep shows zero 'hq-fix'/'hq-gbl' leftovers outside Trash.

title: Bug: bulk_update_todos double-emits tags under ALLOW_ALL - valid_tags already includes created_tags, then existing+created concatenates again
description: Found by hq-gbl.5 (tests/unit/test_write_input_matrix.py, worked around with a seeded existing-tags mock): tools_helpers/bulk_operations.py:44-45 _validate_tags_with_policy maps existing=result.valid_tags, but under ALLOW_ALL TagValidationResult.valid_tags already includes created_tags; bulk_operations.py:101's existing+created then double-counts - bulk_update_todos(tags='a,b') emits tag string 'a, b, a, b' to AppleScript. Things may dedupe on its side (verify live with a throwaway) but the emitted payload is wrong. Check WriteOperations' equivalent path for the same defect. FIX: dedupe (existing = [t for t in valid if t not in created]) or use valid_tags alone; unit test asserting the emitted script's tag list; check tests/regression/test_tags.py's ALLOW_ALL coverage. CHANGELOG.

title: Bug: five list tools crash (ToolError) on bogus mode instead of returning invalid_mode read error
description: Found by hq-gbl.4 (tests/unit/test_read_input_matrix.py): get_inbox/get_today/get_upcoming/get_anytime/get_someday do not pre-validate mode (server.py:1265-1424) - a bogus mode string reaches ResponseMode(...) unguarded, raising an unhandled ValueError surfaced by FastMCP as ToolError with no structured_content, while get_todos/get_projects/get_areas/search_todos/search_advanced return the canonical read_error('invalid_mode', ...) (server.py:293-408). FIX: add the same _validate_mode pre-check to the five list tools (shared helper); update the matrix CASES expectations from tool_error() to read_error('invalid_mode') for those five; CHANGELOG.

title: Bug: operation_queue singleton binds its worker task to the first event loop - queue_status/get_server_capabilities hang when called from a second loop
description: Found by hq-gbl.16: src/things_mcp/operation_queue.py get_operation_queue()'s module-level _global_queue binds its worker asyncio.Task to the loop running at first creation; a later call from a DIFFERENT event loop (e.g. an MCP client doing asyncio.run per call - reproduced live with two bare sequential asyncio.run-wrapped queue_status calls) hangs indefinitely instead of raising: _worker_task.done() polled across loops never resolves. Affects queue_status and get_server_capabilities (anything touching the queue). FIX: in get_operation_queue()/OperationQueue.start(), detect that the bound loop is not the currently-running loop (worker task's get_loop() vs asyncio.get_running_loop()) and recreate the queue/worker on the current loop (or make the singleton per-loop via WeakKeyDictionary). Unit test simulating two sequential asyncio.run calls (must complete, with a timeout guard). The workaround batching in tests/regression/test_utility_tools.py (single shared-loop async test) can then be relaxed. CHANGELOG.
notes: Reviewer refinement (hq-gbl.16): the hang manifests at the SECOND event loop's shutdown/teardown after get_operation_queue() (operation_queue.py:441) restarts the worker cross-loop - operation_queue.py:130 create_task binds the worker to the first loop; .done() itself is not the blocking call. Repro: 2x sequential asyncio.run(get_operation_queue()) hangs at second-loop teardown (15s timeout). Also fold in: pyproject sets pytest timeout=300 but pytest-timeout is NOT installed in the uv venv, so a regression here hangs the suite - add pytest-timeout to dev deps as part of this fix. And correct tests/regression/test_utility_tools.py's workaround docstring mechanism when fixing.

title: Bug: summary-mode preview items are {id,name}, contradicting the documented SUMMARY field set {uuid,title,status,tags,dueDate}
description: Found by hq-gbl.13 (strict xfail TestModes::test_todo_field_sets[summary] in tests/regression/test_list_tools.py): context_manager.py:265-291 _summarize_todos/_summarize_projects/_summarize_search_results build preview items keyed {id,name}, while CLAUDE.md's 'Todo field lists per mode' documents SUMMARY as uuid/title/status/tags/dueDate. Verified live on get_todos(mode='summary') and get_anytime(mode='summary'). FIX: emit the documented keys (uuid/title/status/tags/dueDate) in the preview rows (breaking change for anyone reading id/name - note in CHANGELOG), or amend CLAUDE.md if {id,name} is the intended contract; align _summarize_projects/_summarize_search_results too; unit tests on the preview shape; flip the strict xfail. CHANGELOG.

title: Bug: THINGS_MCP_TAG_CREATION_POLICY env var is dead - pydantic validator ordering makes ai_can_create_tags always win (FILTER_SILENT/FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN unreachable via env)
description: Found by hq-gbl.11: config.py:339-381 - THINGS_MCP_AI_CAN_CREATE_TAGS (declared first) is validated before tag_creation_policy, so tag_creation_policy's before-validator sees ai_can_create_tags already present and overrides the policy from it alone; setting THINGS_MCP_TAG_CREATION_POLICY (env or env_file) never takes effect, making FILTER_SILENT and FAIL_ON_UNKNOWN unreachable via environment configuration. FIX: rework the cross-sync validators (e.g. model_validator(mode='after') that reconciles both with explicit precedence: explicit policy wins over derived-from-bool), unit tests constructing ThingsMCPConfig from env for each of the 4 policies asserting .tag_creation_policy AND .ai_can_create_tags, plus precedence when both are set. Update tests/regression/test_tags.py policy matrix to then cover all 4 policies. CHANGELOG.

title: Bug: add_project with unknown area_title returns APPLESCRIPT_ERROR but still creates the project (no rollback)
description: Found by hq-gbl.10 (strict xfail test_area_title_unknown in tests/regression/test_projects_areas.py): scheduling/todo_operations.py _build_create_project_script runs 'make new project' and 'set area of ...' in one try block - when the area lookup fails, the response is success=False/APPLESCRIPT_ERROR yet the project persists in Things (silent orphan; leaked 4 projects during test iteration until the test learned to track them). Same risk likely applies to unknown area_id and to add_todo's equivalent script if structured the same - check both. FIX: pre-resolve area_title/area_id via things.py BEFORE the write (mirroring add_todo's list_title resolution, return NOT_FOUND/AMBIGUOUS_TARGET without creating anything), or delete the just-created project in an on-error handler. Unit tests asserting no 'make new project' is emitted (or the rollback delete IS emitted) on unknown area; flip the strict xfail. CHANGELOG.

title: Bug: intermittent bulk_move partial failures under max_concurrent>1 - Things errors under rapid AppleEvents bypass executor retry
description: CORRECTED DIAGNOSIS (hq-gbl.9 review): AppleScript IS serialized process-wide - AppleScriptExecutor._applescript_lock (services/applescript/executor.py:22) is acquired at :95 around every osascript call; applescript_manager.py:48's _applescript_lock is dead code (remove it). The real defect chain: (a) Things 3 intermittently errors under rapid back-to-back AppleEvents (serialized but unpaced bursts; max_concurrent=1 passes clean); (b) executor retry only fires on returncode!=0, while in-script 'on error' handlers return 'ERROR: ...' with returncode 0, bypassing retry and surfacing as failed_moves. FIX: treat 'ERROR:'-prefixed stdout as retryable in the executor (bounded, with small backoff/pacing), remove the dead lock in applescript_manager.py, then tighten/remove _bulk_move_tolerating_concurrency_race in tests/regression/test_bulk_and_move.py (at minimum make it match the transient error signature). Unit tests for the retry-on-ERROR-stdout path. CHANGELOG.

title: Bug: move_record/bulk_move_records - 'logbook' and 'trash' pass validation but are never routed (always INVALID_DESTINATION)
description: Found by hq-gbl.9 (strict xfails test_move_to_logbook/test_move_to_trash/TestBulkMoveRecordsDestinations::test_to_trash in tests/regression/test_bulk_and_move.py). move_operations.py _validate_destination accepts 'logbook'/'trash' but _execute_move's if/elif routing has no branch for them, so the call always returns INVALID_DESTINATION after validation succeeded. FIX: route trash to the existing move-to-Trash script and logbook to complete-the-todo (or reject both at validation with a clear message if intentionally unsupported - then update CLAUDE.md's destination table). Unit tests on routing; flip the strict xfails. CHANGELOG.

title: Bug: add_todo/update_todo when='YYYY-MM-DD@HH:MM' silently drops the @HH:MM reminder time on the AppleScript path
description:
Found by hq-gbl.7 regression tests (strict xfail TestAddTodoWhen::test_when_iso_date_with_time_sets_reminder in tests/regression/test_todo_create_delete.py). when='YYYY-MM-DD@HH:MM' passes validation (parameter_validator accepts it) but locale_aware_dates.normalize_date_input, used by the AppleScript scheduling path (schedule_todo_reliable), extracts only Y/M/D - the @HH:MM is silently dropped, no reminder is set, and start stays 'Someday'. The Things URL scheme DOES support when=YYYY-MM-DD@HH:MM natively (sets a reminder).
FIX: route date+time when values through the URL scheme (like evening), or set the reminder via AppleScript if possible - probe live first with a throwaway to-do (prefix 'hq-gbl-fix '); add unit tests asserting the route/emitted payload for when with @HH:MM on add_todo/update_todo/bulk_update_todos; flip the strict xfail (it will XPASS-fail until removed). CHANGELOG Unreleased entry.

title: Bug: add_todo/update_todo when='today' via AppleScript schedule verb leaves start='Someday' (absent from get_anytime), unlike the URL-scheme path
description:
Found by the hq-gbl seed oracle (hq-gbl.6) and confirmed live by the reviewer: add_todo(when='today') on the AppleScript path (scheduling.method='applescript_relative', script `schedule theTodo for (current date)`) yields things.get start='Someday', start_date=today -> appears in things.today()/get_today but NOT in things.anytime()/get_anytime. The same when='today' sent via the URL scheme (e.g. add_todo(when='today', checklist_items=[...]) or when='evening') yields start='Anytime', start_date=today and appears in both. Things' own Anytime list contains Today items, so the AppleScript path's result is the odd one out (it corresponds to Things' unconfirmed/yellow-dot scheduled state). Read-only census of the user's real Today list shows both states coexist (83 Anytime / 47 Someday), so this is not purely cosmetic.
FIX OPTIONS (pick after a live probe): (a) after `schedule ... for (current date)` also `move theTodo to list "Today"` or set `activation date`; (b) route when='today' through the URL scheme like evening; (c) document. Add unit tests on the emitted script, then remove the XFAILS entry ("get_anytime","today","must") in tests/regression/test_seed_oracle.py (strict xfail - it will XPASS-fail until removed). Verify live with throwaway to-dos prefixed 'hq-gbl-fix '. CHANGELOG Unreleased entry. Related: hq-z5d (when='anytime' lands in Someday).

Also one to-do inside the completed sandbox project is NOT created (TARGET_COMPLETED) - instead create it before completing? No: the harness already completes that project empty; leave it.

3. test_seed_oracle.py: one parametrized test per (tool, class) asserting presence/absence by uuid using mode='minimal', limit=500 (and offset paging where available) - this IS the list-tool membership regression. Where a read lags a URL-scheme write, use read_back polling before asserting.

title: Release v1.7.0: tag, GitHub release, CI publish watch, .mcpb upload, smoke test, close GH #9/#10 (HUMAN GO-AHEAD REQUIRED)
description:
Outward-facing: publishes to PyPI and GitHub and posts on public issues. The orchestrator must get explicit human confirmation before dispatching this bead.

Steps (per CLAUDE.md Release Process):
1. Ensure main is clean and pushed (`git status`, `git pull --rebase`, `git push origin main`).
2. `git tag v1.7.0 && git push origin v1.7.0`.
3. `gh release create v1.7.0 --title "v1.7.0 - <title>" --notes "$(sed -n '/## \[1.7.0\]/,/## \[/p' CHANGELOG.md | head -n -1)"`.
4. Watch CI: `gh run watch "$(gh run list --workflow=publish.yml --limit 1 --json databaseId --jq '.[0].databaseId')" --exit-status` - must be green through verify-pypi. If publish-to-pypi fails with the OIDC 403, follow the CLAUDE.md note (trusted publisher on the mcp-server-things project) and re-run; do not twine upload unless CI is broken and the human says so.
5. `scripts/build_mcpb.sh` then `gh release upload v1.7.0 dist/mcp-server-things-1.7.0.mcpb`.
6. Smoke test the published package: `uvx --refresh --python-preference only-managed --python 3.12 mcp-server-things@1.7.0 --version` prints 1.7.0 and `... doctor` passes (PyPI index may lag a few minutes - retry with --refresh).
7. Reply on GitHub issue #10: summarise the three fixes (read-path title protection; shared escaper preserving newlines in add/update todo/project incl. bulk), note the fix is in v1.7.0, thank the reporter. Reply on issue #9: list tools now return to-dos only (projects via include_projects), heading/headingTitle/type/start/projectTitle fields, add_todo(heading=...) works on every path, new get_project_headings, update_todo(heading=...), and state plainly that creating/renaming/deleting headings is not possible via Things' public AppleScript/URL APIs (headings can only be seeded at project creation via the URL scheme's ##Heading lines). Then close both issues (`gh issue close N --comment ...` or close after commenting).
8. `bd sync --flush-only` and commit .beads/ per session policy.

Done criteria: tag + release exist, CI green through verify-pypi, .mcpb attached, uvx smoke test passes, both issues commented and closed, beads synced.

title: Sweep S5: URL-scheme update tools fail fast when the Things auth token is missing
description:
Input (write-side sweep): services/applescript_manager.py:72-94 loads the Things URL-scheme auth token from optional files and returns None with only logger.debug when missing; utils/formatters.py:29 then omits auth-token from the URL; execute_url_scheme (applescript_manager.py:126-145) reports success whenever `open -g` exits 0, which it does even when Things rejects the URL. Result: add_checklist_items / prepend_checklist_items / replace_checklist_items (and any future things:///update user such as update_todo(heading=...) in hq-f0w.7) return {"success": true, ...} while nothing happened, if the token is not configured. (things:///add does NOT need a token - do not gate it.)

Steps:
1. In the URL-scheme execution path, when the action requires auth (update, update-project, and any other token-requiring command per Things URL scheme docs - enumerate them in a constant) and the token is None, return {"success": False, "error": "Things URL-scheme auth token not configured", "hint": "<the exact file locations / env var the loader checks, and where to find the token in Things: Settings > General > Enable Things URLs > Manage>"} WITHOUT invoking `open`. Acceptance: add_checklist_items with no token returns success=false and execute_script/`open` is never called.
2. Surface the same condition in `mcp-server-things doctor` if not already (the 1.6.0 doctor has an 'optional Things URL-scheme auth token file' check - make its WARN text name the tools that need it).
3. Unit tests: each checklist tool + the URL-scheme executor: token missing -> structured error, no `open`; token present -> URL contains auth-token=...; things:///add with no token still proceeds.
4. Docs: README (Configuration / Troubleshooting) and CLAUDE.md checklist section: token requirement and setup; tool docstrings for the three checklist tools mention it.
5. `pytest tests/unit -q` green.

Done criteria: token-missing path returns an actionable error for every token-requiring tool; add path unaffected; tests + docs in place; suite green.

Edge cases: token file present but empty/whitespace -> treat as missing; token loaded once at startup vs lazily - keep current behaviour but make sure a token added after startup is picked up on next call if the loader is cheap (optional; document whichever you choose).
notes: Reviewer follow-ups: (1) checklist tools drop the 'hint' field from the executor error (todo_operations.py ~:394,443,484 forward only 'error') - one-line pass-through would help, relevant to hq-f0w.7 too; (2) reliable_scheduling.py:161-173 has an unused ungated things:///update path (dead code); (3) .env.example:30-31 still says the token is used for all URL-scheme ops incl. add-with-checklist - nit.

title: Sweep C3/C4: update_project ignores canceled and sets completion date instead of status
description:
Input (write-side sweep, confirmed by rendering scripts):
- C3: server.py:874,893 declares and forwards update_project(canceled=...), but scheduling/todo_operations.py:791 reads only completed = kwargs.get('completed'); `canceled` is never read and no AppleScript is emitted. update_project(id=P, canceled="true") returns success with the project still open.
- C4: todo_operations.py:836-840 emits `set completion date of targetProject to (current date)` for completed=true (and a 'missing value' reset for false) instead of `set status of targetProject to completed/open`; the todo path (_build_update_script :566-573) uses `status`. Setting completion date alone does not reliably move a project to the Logbook.

Steps:
1. In update_project (todo_operations.py ~:791-840): read `canceled = kwargs.get('canceled')`; emit `set status of targetProject to canceled` / `completed` / `open` using the same precedence and true/false string handling as _build_update_script :566-573 (canceled takes precedence over completed when both given; 'false' reopens). Remove the completion-date mutation. Acceptance: rendered script for completed='true' contains `set status of targetProject to completed`; for canceled='true' contains `to canceled`; for completed='false' contains `to open`.
2. Check bulk/other project paths for the same pattern (grep 'completion date' in src/) and align them.
3. Unit tests (tests/unit/test_project_*.py or new tests/unit/test_update_project_status.py): render the script for each of completed true/false, canceled true/false, both set; assert exact status statements and no `completion date`. Add a test that update_project forwards `canceled` (sentinel reaches the script).
4. Docs: update_project docstring in server.py and CLAUDE.md Working with Projects: completed/canceled semantics (canceled wins; 'false' reopens).
5. `pytest tests/unit -q` green.

Done criteria: real Things 3 check - create a throwaway project, update_project(canceled='true') -> things.get(uuid)['status'] == 'canceled'; update_project(canceled='false') -> 'incomplete'; update_project(completed='true') -> 'completed'; then trash it; suite green.

Edge cases: completed='false' and canceled='true' together; values 'True'/'1'/'yes' - follow whatever the todo path accepts and keep them identical.
notes: Reviewer scope notes: (1) update_project(canceled=False) alone -> open, diverges from update_todo where canceled=False alone is a no-op - consider aligning todo/bulk in a follow-up; (2) server string->bool conversion (.lower()=='true') means canceled='yes'/'1' becomes False and reopens - stricter validator would help; (3) dead AppleScriptManager.update_project_direct has completed-wins precedence, no callers.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS (807 passed). Real-Things: canceled->canceled, canceled=false->incomplete, completed->completed on throwaway project; trashed.

title: GH#9 item 3b + sweep S2/S3: add_todo heading/list_title honoured on every path; escape list_id
description:
Input: GH #9 item 3 (write side, creation). add_todo declares `heading` (server.py:387, threaded at :425; advertised in CLAUDE.md ~:461-463) but scheduling/todo_operations.py:148-166 only passes it on the URL-scheme branch, taken only when checklist_items is non-empty; the default AppleScript path (_build_create_todo_script :64-66) has no heading argument and drops it silently. Things 3 AppleScript has no heading class (sdef confirms), so the URL scheme `add` command with `heading` (title of an existing heading in the target project) / `heading-id` is the only way to place a new to-do under a heading.

Sweep findings folded in (same shape - parameter honoured only on the checklist/URL branch):
- S2: add_todo(list_title=...) is forwarded by server.py:434 but todo_operations.py:143-152 only reads list_title inside _add_todo_with_checklist; the AppleScript branch reads only kwargs 'project'/'list_id'/'area', so a todo created with list_title and no checklist lands in the Inbox with success:true.
- S3: todo_operations.py:97 interpolates list_id raw into `set project of newTodo to project id "..."` (not escaped, unlike area at :94) and always assumes a project - an area UUID errors even though server.py:386 documents list_id as 'ID of project/area'.

Steps:
1. In todo_operations.py add_todo: take the URL-scheme branch whenever `heading` is truthy OR checklist_items is non-empty (the existing _add_todo_with_checklist / URL builder already sets params['heading'] at ~:254-255 - generalise/rename so an empty checklist is fine). Acceptance: add_todo(title=..., list_id=P, heading="Research") with no checklist emits a things:///add URL containing heading=Research and list-id=P.
2. Validation: if `heading` is given but neither list_id nor list_title is provided, return {"success": False, "error": "heading requires a target project (list_id or list_title)"} without calling Things. If Things ignores the heading because it does not exist in that project, the to-do still lands in the project - document this (URL scheme gives no error); pre-check via things.tasks(type='heading', project=<resolved project id>) and include a `warnings` entry when no heading with that title exists.
3. list_title on the AppleScript branch: resolve list_title to a project or area id via things.py (things.projects()/things.areas() exact-title match; if ambiguous (>1 match) return a structured error listing the ids; if no match return a structured error) and then emit the correct `set project of newTodo to project id "..."` or `set area of newTodo to area id "..."`. Acceptance: add_todo(title='X', list_title='<existing project title>') with no checklist places the todo in that project.
4. list_id: escape it with the shared escaper (no raw interpolation) and decide project-vs-area by looking it up via things.get(list_id) (type 'project' -> project id ..., type 'area'/area record -> area id ...); unknown id -> structured error before any AppleScript write. Acceptance: an area uuid passed as list_id places the todo in the area.
5. Make sure the post-create id lookup used by the URL-scheme path still works for the no-checklist case, and that tags/when/deadline/notes/list are all forwarded on this path exactly as on the checklist path (newlines in notes percent-encoded as %0A - formatters.py:42 already does this).
6. Unit tests: add_todo with heading and no checklist uses the URL-scheme executor (mock it) and the URL contains heading + list-id; heading without project returns the structured error; heading + checklist still works (regression); list_title (project) and list_title (area) resolve correctly on the AppleScript path (mock things.projects/areas); ambiguous/unknown list_title -> structured error; list_id pointing at an area -> `set area of`; list_id with a double quote cannot break the script.
7. Docs: CLAUDE.md + README add_todo docs: heading must already exist in the target project; created via URL scheme (no auth token needed for `add` - confirm from utils/formatters.py / applescript_manager.py and state precisely); list_title now works on all paths.
8. `pytest tests/unit -q` green.

Done criteria: real Things 3 verification - using an existing project that has a heading (find one via things.tasks(type='heading'); if none exists, create a throwaway project with add_project whose todos payload uses the URL-scheme `##Heading` line syntax if the current add_project supports it, else pick any project and create the heading... NOTE: headings cannot be created via AppleScript - if no project with a heading exists and add_project cannot seed one, state that in the bead notes and verify the URL contents only), call add_todo(title='heading test', list_id=P, heading=<title>) with no checklist, confirm via things.get(uuid)['heading_title'] that it landed under the heading; call add_todo(title='lt test', list_title=<project title>) and confirm things.get(uuid)['project'] == P; then trash the todos; unit suite green.

Edge cases: heading title containing & / ? # % (must be percent-encoded); heading + when/deadline together; heading passed with list_title instead of list_id; list_title that matches both a project and an area (report ambiguity).
notes: Reviewer notes: _resolve_list_title swallows things.py exceptions into 'no match' (message could say DB unreadable); fallback:True from _resolve_list_id not surfaced in response (log only).
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on 2nd review (826 on base; 1060 after rebase incl. a 3-line test rename reconciliation with hq-f0w.12). Live: heading placement, list_title->project, list_id area, URL list-id area all verified; items trashed.

title: GH#9 item 3a + sweep C1-C3: rewrite convert_todo/convert_project against the real things.py key set (type, heading, start, stop_date, project_title, checklist flag)
description:
Input: GH #9 item 3 (read side) - callers cannot tell which heading a task sits under, nor distinguish to-do/project/heading. tools_helpers/helpers.py:114-148 ToolsHelpers.convert_todo drops things.py's `type`, `heading` (uuid) and `heading_title`. Read-side sweep found the converter is keyed to fields things.py never emits:
- C2: helpers.py:132,133,137 read completion_date / cancellation_date / area - live frequency over 3699 rows: 0. The real key is `stop_date` (100% of rows; carries both completion and cancellation time, disambiguated by `status`). So every completed/canceled todo comes back with NO completion date. convert_project has the same bug at :170-171. Todos have no `area` key (0/1699); projects do (and also `area_title`, dropped).
- C1: helpers.py:138 copies `checklist` as if it were a list; things.py emits a BOOL has-checklist flag (live: all 16 rows with the key are True). Default get_todos path therefore returns "checklist": true where the schema promises items; only include_items overwrites it (read_operations.py:207).
- C3: also dropped: `start` (the actual Inbox/Anytime/Someday state - the only way to tell where a todo lives; distinct from start_date: live row start='Someday', start_date='2026-08-08'), `stop_date`, `project_title` (present on 1006/1699 incomplete todos - callers currently get an opaque uuid), `index`, `today_index`. convert_area requests `tags` which areas never have (permanent []).
Real things.py to-do keys: uuid,type,title,status,notes,start,start_date,deadline,stop_date,created,modified,index,today_index,tags,project,project_title,heading,heading_title,checklist. Capture the real key sets for project/area/tag/heading the same way (read-only python) before editing.
Also: get_todos(project_uuid=...) uses the AppleScript read path (read_operations.py:158-160) which has no heading concept.

Steps:
1. Rewrite convert_todo (helpers.py) to emit, in the existing camelCase convention: uuid, title, type (default 'to-do'), status, notes, start (verbatim things.py value: 'Inbox'|'Anytime'|'Someday'), startDate, deadline, completionDate (= stop_date when status=='completed' else None), cancellationDate (= stop_date when status=='canceled' else None), created, modified, tags, project, projectTitle, heading, headingTitle, hasChecklist (bool from things.py 'checklist'), checklist (list - ONLY when real items were fetched via things.checklist_items; otherwise omit the key or None - pick one and document), index, todayIndex. Keep every currently-emitted key name that is correct so nothing downstream breaks (grep for consumers of each key: context_manager.py mode field sets, server.py, tests). Remove `area` from convert_todo. Acceptance: for a realistic things.py row every listed key is present with the right value.
2. convert_project: completionDate/cancellationDate from stop_date by status; add areaTitle, type; keep area. convert_area: drop the phantom tags lookup (or keep it only if things.areas(include_items=...) can return tags - verify). Acceptance: same as 1 for projects/areas.
3. context_manager.py mode field sets (~:495-503): add type, start, projectTitle, heading, headingTitle to STANDARD; MINIMAL must keep at least uuid,title,status,type,start,project so a minimal result can still locate a todo; remove `area` from the todo STANDARD set. Document the resulting per-mode field lists in CLAUDE.md Context Budget Guidelines.
4. read_operations.py get_todos AppleScript path (project_uuid branch, ~:158-175): after the AppleScript fetch succeeds, best-effort enrich each returned todo with heading/headingTitle/projectTitle/start by building a uuid->row map from things.todos(project=project_uuid) (try/except, log at debug on failure, never fail the call). Acceptance: a todo under a heading returned by get_todos(project_uuid=...) carries headingTitle.
5. Unit tests: tests/unit for convert_todo/convert_project/convert_area using a realistic row captured from things.py (hardcode the captured dict in the test); completionDate/cancellationDate derivation by status; hasChecklist bool vs checklist list; get_todos enrichment with things.todos mocked; context_manager mode retention per mode. Update tests/unit/test_structured_output.py and any test asserting exact key sets.
6. Docs: CLAUDE.md Structured Output/Context Budget + README field docs: list the todo fields per mode; note start vs startDate; note heading info comes from the Things database and AppleScript-sourced reads are enriched best-effort. Add a docs/UPGRADING.md line: new fields added, `area` removed from todo dicts (was always null), `checklist` now only a list when items were fetched (was a stray bool).
7. `pytest tests/unit -q` green.

Done criteria: real Things 3 check - pick a completed todo, a canceled todo, a Someday todo with a start_date, a todo under a heading, a todo with a checklist: convert each via get_todo_by_id / get_todos and confirm completionDate/cancellationDate/start/headingTitle/projectTitle/hasChecklist are correct; unit suite green.

Edge cases: todos not under any heading -> heading=None, headingTitle=None (keys present, values null); projects/headings passed through convert_todo (include_projects=True from hq-f0w.3) carry type='project'; rows missing `start` (mocks) -> None.
notes: Reviewer follow-ups: (1) todos under a heading have project/projectTitle None from things.py - convert_todo could use _resolve_heading_project (read_operations ~:50-70); ties to hq-f0w.6; (2) enrichment uses things.todos(project=) default status incomplete so completed todos not enriched; _get_todos_sync project_uuid fallback ignores status - hq-nxu.8; (3) enrichment is a sync sqlite call on the event loop; (4) convert_applescript_todo still lacks type - hq-nxu.8; (5) context_manager.py ~:642 get_usage_recommendations field_sets stale - hq-nxu.7; (6) helpers.py convert_todo docstring claims camelCase fallback it doesn't implement; CLAUDE.md says checklist list only with include_items but get_todo_by_id always emits it.

title: GH#9 items 1-2 + sweep: list tools (incl. get_trash) return to-dos only; headings never, projects opt-in
description:
Input: GH #9 items 1 and 2 - get_anytime/get_someday (and get_today, found during investigation) include projects and headings. Root cause: tools_helpers/read_operations.py calls things.anytime() (:568), things.someday() (:611), things.today() (:520), things.upcoming() (:544), things.inbox() (:498) with no type filter; things.py's tasks() returns type in {'to-do','project','heading'} and these wrappers accept a type= kwarg. Live DB today: anytime 1175 = 1106 to-do + 39 project + 30 heading; someday 77 = 54 + 23 project; today 130 = 114 + 16 project. Read-side sweep C6: get_trash (read_operations.py:704, things.trash() no type=) leaks projects too - live 1309 to-dos + 8 projects, docstring says 'Get trashed todos'.

Design decision (already made, do not re-litigate): headings are NEVER returned by these list tools. Projects are excluded by default and opt-in via a new `include_projects: bool = False` parameter on get_today, get_upcoming, get_anytime, get_someday, get_trash (inbox cannot contain projects - always type='to-do', no flag).

Steps:
1. In read_operations.py, change the six _get_*_sync helpers (inbox, today, upcoming, anytime, someday, trash) to call things.<list>(type='to-do') by default; when include_projects is true, fetch with no type filter and drop items whose type == 'heading' (or fetch to-do + project separately and merge, preserving things.py order). Keep the existing filter_someday_project_tasks / include_project_tasks behaviour and get_trash's pre-limit total_count unchanged. Acceptance: with include_projects=False the result never contains type 'project' or 'heading'.
2. Thread `include_projects: bool = False` through the async wrappers and the MCP tool signatures in server.py for get_today, get_upcoming, get_anytime, get_someday, get_trash (follow the pattern used for get_someday's include_project_tasks). Update each tool docstring: headings are never returned; projects only with include_projects=true, matching the Things app's list views. 3. Unit tests (new tests/unit/test_list_type_filtering.py): mock things.anytime/someday/today/upcoming/inbox/trash to return a mix of to-do/project/heading dicts; assert default excludes project+heading for all six; assert include_projects=True includes projects but still excludes headings; assert things.<fn> is called with type='to-do' by default (filter in the query, not only post-hoc). Update tests/unit/test_trash_pagination.py mocks to include a project. Acceptance: tests fail on the old code, pass on the new.
4. Run `pytest tests/unit -q`; run `python scripts/gen_manifest_tools.py --check` (if drift, --write and include the result). Acceptance: green, manifest in sync.
5. Update CLAUDE.md (Structured Output / Someday section) and README tool docs with one short paragraph on the new default + flag; add a line to docs/UPGRADING.md 'behavioural changes to review'.

Done criteria: real Things 3 check via python snippet calling the sync helpers: get_anytime returns only type=='to-do' items (~1106 not 1175 on the dev DB), get_someday ~54 not 77, get_today ~114 not 130, get_trash ~1309 not 1317; include_projects=True adds back only projects; unit suite green; docs updated.

Edge cases: items lacking a 'type' key (mocked tests) are treated as to-do; things.py version must accept type= (verified on the installed version; if a call rejects it, filter post-hoc and note it).

title: GH#10 bug 3 + sweep C1/C2: one shared AppleScript escaper that preserves newlines; fix .strip('"') re-wrap sites
description:
Input: GH #10 bug 3 - add_project/update_project (and, untested by the reporter but equally affected, add_todo/update_todo) store multi-line notes with every newline collapsed to a single space. Root cause: utils/applescript_utils.py:33-35 AppleScriptTemplates.escape_string does .replace('\n',' ').replace('\r',' ') before the ASCII<32 strip at :38. Call sites: scheduling/todo_operations.py:82 (add_todo), :532 (update_todo), :669 (add_project), :818 (update_project). Areas are unaffected (no notes). The URL-scheme path (utils/formatters.py:42, %0A) and services/applescript_manager.py:535 (.replace('\n','\\n')) already preserve newlines - use the latter as the model.

Sweep findings folded in (same root cause - two divergent escapers):
- C2: tools_helpers/helpers.py:14-27 ToolsHelpers.escape_applescript_string handles only backslash and quote; a raw newline passes through into an AppleScript string literal (syntax error - AppleScript string literals cannot span lines). Used by tools_helpers/bulk_operations.py:123,127 (bulk title/notes) and services/write_operations.py:449,507 (add_tags/remove_tags tag strings).
- C1: bulk_operations.py:123-127 does escape_applescript_string(x).strip('"') then re-wraps in quotes; for a value ending in a double quote the escaped payload ends in \" so .strip('"') leaves a dangling backslash that eats the closing quote -> unbalanced script. Confirmed: title 'Say "hi"' emits `set name of targetTodo to "Say \"hi\"` (no terminating quote). Same anti-pattern at write_operations.py:507 (remove_tags remaining-tag string).

Steps:
1. Make ONE escaper the source of truth: AppleScriptTemplates.escape_string (utils/applescript_utils.py) escapes backslash first, then double quote, then maps '\n' -> backslash+n, '\r' -> backslash+r, '\t' -> backslash+t (AppleScript interprets these inside a double-quoted literal), strips remaining control chars < 0x20, and returns the value wrapped in double quotes (keep current return contract - check every caller expects the quoted form). Make ToolsHelpers.escape_applescript_string delegate to it (same return contract as today - check whether callers expect quoted or unquoted and adapt the callers rather than keeping two semantics; document the contract in both docstrings). Acceptance: escape_string('Line one.\n\nLine two.') == '"Line one.\\n\\nLine two."' (literal backslash-n pairs); escape_string('a"b\\c') escapes quote and backslash correctly; no raw newline can appear inside an emitted string literal from either function.
2. Remove every `.strip('"')` + manual re-wrap pattern: bulk_operations.py:123-127 and write_operations.py:507 (and any other site found by `grep -n "strip('\"')" src/`) must use the escaper's quoted output directly. Acceptance: grep returns zero hits.
3. Unit tests (tests/unit/test_applescript_utils.py or alongside existing escape tests): single newline, double newline, \r\n, tab, mixed quotes+newlines, value ending in a double quote, injection attempt `" & do shell script "echo pwned" & "` stays a plain string; script-builder tests asserting _build_create_todo_script, the project create/update builders (scheduling/todo_operations.py), _build_bulk_update_script (bulk_operations.py) and the add_tags/remove_tags scripts emit balanced quotes and the escaped newline sequence (not a space, not a raw newline). Strengthen tests/unit/test_edge_cases.py:162 test_newlines_in_notes and tests/unit/test_tools.py:37 test_escape_applescript_string to inspect the escaped output/generated script rather than only success=True. A balanced-quotes helper assertion (count of unescaped double quotes in the emitted script is even) is cheap and catches C1-class bugs generally - add it and apply to every builder test you touch.
4. Run `pytest tests/unit -q`. Acceptance: all pass.
5. Verify against real Things 3: create a throwaway project via add_project(notes="Line one.\n\nLine two.\n\nLine three.") and a throwaway todo via add_todo with the same notes; read both back via things.py (things.get(uuid)['notes']) and assert the newlines are present; update_project/update_todo with new multi-line notes and re-check; bulk_update_todos on the throwaway todo with title 'Say "hi"' and notes 'a\nb' and confirm both applied; then trash all throwaway items. Record observed values in the bead notes (`bd update <id> --notes`).

Done criteria: all four notes-writing ops preserve \n and \n\n end-to-end on a real Things 3; bulk_update_todos with a trailing-quote title and multi-line notes works; one escaper implementation remains (the other delegates); new tests assert the escaped form and balanced quotes; unit suite green.

Edge cases: notes=None / empty string; notes with only whitespace/newlines; CRLF input; titles with newlines (shared escaper - same treatment, fine); tag names containing quotes in add_tags/remove_tags.
notes:
Observed real-Things values: add_project/add_todo/update_project/update_todo notes read back as 'Line one.

title: Shield boot path from things.py's unbounded module-level Group Containers glob
description:
INPUT: src/things_mcp/tools.py:7 (`import things`) and src/things_mcp/tools_helpers/read_operations.py:8 (`import things`), which transitively trigger venv/.../site-packages/things/database.py:31-34:
  try:
      DEFAULT_FILEPATH = next(glob.iglob(os.path.expanduser(DEFAULT_FILEPATH_31616502)))
  except StopIteration:
      DEFAULT_FILEPATH = os.path.expanduser(DEFAULT_FILEPATH_31516502)
This module-level glob runs unconditionally, synchronously, and without a timeout the first time `things` is imported anywhere in the process -- which today happens at server import time (server.py -> tools.py), before ThingsMCPServer.__init__ even starts, and before most boot_marker phases fire. It walks ~/Library/Group Containers/JLMPQHK86H.com.culturedcode.ThingsMac/ThingsData-*/... on disk. If that path is slow to stat (external/synced volume asleep, FileVault unlock delay, Spotlight/mds or Time Machine snapshot contention around overnight hours), this call can block the entire stdio handshake indefinitely with zero stderr output -- this is a confirmed audit finding from hq-l1a.3, identified as the top hang hypothesis.

WORK:
1. In src/things_mcp/boot_trace.py or server.py, bracket the point where `things` first gets imported with boot_marker calls (e.g. `boot_marker("things-import-start")` / `boot_marker("things-import-done")`) so a future hang at this exact spot is visible in the boot trace even before the full fix lands.
2. Defer the first `import things` so it no longer executes synchronously on the module-import path that gates the stdio handshake: perform it lazily (first real use) inside a bounded operation, e.g. run the import via `asyncio.to_thread` (or a plain `threading.Thread` with `.join(timeout=...)` given this executes before any event loop exists in some call paths) with a hard timeout (a few seconds, configurable), and raise/log a clear diagnostic (not a silent hang) if the timeout is exceeded, rather than letting the client's 60s connect timeout be the only signal.
3. Do not change read/write behavior or the public ThingsTools/ReadOperations API -- only change *when* and *how safely* the `things` import happens.
4. Add a unit test (tests/unit) that simulates a slow `things` import (e.g. monkeypatch `importlib.import_module` or the glob call to sleep past the timeout) and asserts the server surfaces a clear timeout error/log line instead of hanging past the configured bound.
5. Run pytest tests/unit and confirm no regressions.

DONE-CRITERIA:
- The `things` import no longer runs unguarded on the synchronous critical path between process start and the stdio handshake being ready to serve.
- A bounded timeout (configurable, sane default e.g. 5-10s) surrounds the import/resolution, with a clear log/stderr message on timeout rather than silent hang.
- boot_trace markers bracket the import so future incidents are diagnosable even if the fix doesn't fully eliminate the underlying OS-level slowness.
- New unit test passes; full tests/unit suite passes with no regressions.
- No change to ThingsTools/ReadOperations public behavior when the import succeeds normally.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add startup watchdog: dump all thread stacks if boot exceeds deadline
description: INPUT: src/things_mcp/main.py, src/things_mcp/server.py; builds on the boot-marker helper from hq-l1a.1. WORK: (1) Immediately after the process-start marker, arm Python's faulthandler: faulthandler.dump_traceback_later(timeout=20, repeat=True, file=sys.stderr) so that if boot stalls anywhere (imports, config, FastMCP init, handshake), every thread's stack is dumped to stderr every 20s — this is the diagnostic the 2026-07-20 outage lacked. (2) Cancel it (faulthandler.cancel_dump_traceback_later()) once the server reaches the point of calling self.mcp.run() AND re-arm is NOT done after that (mcp.run blocks for the server's lifetime by design; a lifetime repeat dump would spam stderr). Decision made here: cancel just before mcp.run() — boot is the window we instrument; if the hang is inside FastMCP's handshake after run() starts, the 20s repeat that fired before cancel still covers it only if cancel happens after handshake — so instead cancel from a FastMCP on-ready hook if available, else cancel after a one-shot 60s window (dump_traceback_later(60, repeat=False) armed at process start, no cancel needed). Implementer: prefer the simplest correct variant — one-shot 25s AND one-shot 55s dumps armed at process start, no cancellation needed; they are no-ops on healthy boots faster than 25s... except dump fires regardless of state; verify a healthy boot (connects in ~1.5s) does NOT emit dumps into normal operation logs in a way that breaks the MCP client — stderr is safe for stdio MCP servers (protocol uses stdout). Document the chosen variant in the bead notes. (3) Make deadline configurable via env THINGS_MCP_BOOT_WATCHDOG_SECS, default 25, 0 disables. EDGE CASES: stderr closed (wrap arm/cancel in try/except); faulthandler already enabled by env. DONE-CRITERIA: unit test that watchdog arms with default deadline, respects env override, and disables at 0; manual verification note that a normal server start still connects and, after the deadline passes with the server healthy, stderr traceback dumps (if any fire) do not corrupt MCP stdout; pytest tests/unit passes.
close_reason: Closed

title: Add timestamped boot-phase markers to stderr from entrypoint
description: INPUT: src/things_mcp/main.py (main(), ServerManager.start), src/things_mcp/server.py (ThingsMCPServer.__init__, run), src/things_mcp/__main__.py. WORK: (1) At the very top of main() in main.py and of server.py main(), before any heavy import or config work, write a timestamped marker line directly to sys.stderr (unbuffered: print(..., file=sys.stderr, flush=True)) — do NOT rely on logging, which is configured later. (2) Emit markers at each boot phase: process-start (entrypoint reached), config-loaded, logging-configured, applescript-manager-ready, tools-registered, calling-mcp.run. Include ISO-8601 timestamp with milliseconds and elapsed-since-start in each line, prefix 'things-mcp boot:'. Markers must appear even when logging config later redirects/filters output. title: Validation gaps: add_tags/remove_tags/move_record accept empty or whitespace todo_id; create_tag lacks minLength - normalize id/name validation across write tools
description: Found by hq-gbl.5: (a) server.py add_tags/remove_tags never validate todo_id non-empty - '' / '   ' pass through as AppleScript 'to do id ""' (update_todo/delete_todo/move_record do validate); (b) move_record's check only rejects falsy, not whitespace-only; (c) create_tag's tag_name has no minLength in the schema ('' succeeds at the boundary; whitespace-only is hq-r87). FIX: add the same non-empty (post-strip) validation + VALIDATION_ERROR shape used by update_todo to add_tags/remove_tags/move_record, and minLength=1 to create_tag's schema; update tests/unit/test_write_input_matrix.py expectations; regenerate tool_schema_snapshot.json. Related: hq-r87, hq-wbm.

title: Bug: _read_result list branch omits requested_mode - 6 read tools break the documented envelope contract
description: Found by hq-gbl.4: server.py:2457-2467 _read_result only sets requested_mode on the dict-response branch; get_logbook/get_due_in_days/get_activating_in_days/get_tags/get_tagged_items/get_recent pass a raw list/ListWithTotal so their structured_content never carries requested_mode, contradicting CLAUDE.md's uniform envelope documentation. FIX: set requested_mode in the list branch too; remove LIST_TOOLS_WITHOUT_REQUESTED_MODE relaxation from tests/unit/test_read_input_matrix.py and assert uniformly; check tests/regression envelope asserts; CHANGELOG.

title: search_advanced: untyped queries only search to-dos; area filter never cascades into project contents - document or extend
description: Found by hq-gbl.15: read_operations.py _search_advanced_sync (~line 1531) routes untyped queries through things.todos() (to-do rows only), so a bare area/start_date/deadline filter can never return a project or heading row until type='project'/'heading' is passed explicitly; and area= matches only items DIRECTLY assigned to the area (things.tasks(area=...)), never to-dos living inside a project that belongs to the area. There is also no project filter parameter on search_advanced. Decide: document these semantics in CLAUDE.md/tool docstring (cheapest), or extend the tool (untyped -> things.tasks(), add project= filter). Regression tests in tests/regression/test_search_and_filters.py already encode observed behavior and would need updating only if semantics change.

title: Bug: create_tag('   ') silently creates a blank-titled tag - whitespace-only name not rejected
description: Found by hq-gbl.11 (strict xfail TestCreateTag::test_whitespace_only_name_rejected in tests/regression/test_tags.py): create_tag('') is rejected but create_tag('   ') passes through, AppleScript trims it, and a blank-titled tag is created in Things (implementer had to hand-delete one during testing). FIX: strip-and-reject whitespace-only tag_name in server.py create_tag (and check add_tags/parse paths treat whitespace-only tag tokens consistently); unit test; flip the xfail. CHANGELOG.

title: Doc drift: preserve_scheduling parameter documented in CLAUDE.md bulk_move_records but does not exist in code
description: Found by hq-gbl.9: CLAUDE.md's bulk_move_records example passes preserve_scheduling=true but no such parameter exists in server.py/move_operations.py. Observed actual semantics (documented in tests/regression/test_bulk_and_move.py docstrings): project moves leave when/deadline untouched; move to today overwrites start_date, leaves deadline. Either implement the parameter or fix CLAUDE.md/README to describe actual behavior.

title: Harness fragility: seed-oracle unpaged limit=500 reads can truncate on large live lists (Anytime holds 1000+)
description: Found by hq-gbl.9: tests/regression/test_seed_oracle.py collects list-tool membership with a single mode=minimal limit=500 fetch; on this live DB Anytime already exceeds 500 items, so a seed item can silently fall outside the window if enough same-state items sort ahead of it (hq-gbl.9 worked around by defaulting its scratch to-dos to when='someday'). FIX: page every oracle collection with offset where the tool supports it, and for tools without offset (get_anytime etc.) either raise the per-call limit to the documented max and assert total<=limit, or fall back to a targeted things.py membership probe when total>limit. Add a note to tests/regression/README.md warning future files to prefer someday/scratch states.

title: Bug: move_record destination 'upcoming' passes validation but Things AppleScript rejects the move
description: Found by hq-gbl.9 (strict xfail test_move_to_upcoming). destination_list='upcoming' passes _validate_destination but Things' AppleScript move verb errors ('Cannot move to-do') -> APPLESCRIPT_ERROR. Things has no direct 'Upcoming' move - an item is Upcoming by having a future start date. FIX: either reject 'upcoming' at validation with a message pointing at update_todo(when=<date>), or implement it as schedule-for-date; update CLAUDE.md destination table; flip the xfail. CHANGELOG.

title: Regression follow-up: when-keyword read-backs for tomorrow/someday are success-only; evening/tonight parametrize lacks token guard
description: From hq-gbl.8 review scope notes: tests/regression/test_update_todo.py test_when_keyword[tomorrow|someday] assert only success+record-exists - add scheduling-state read-backs (start_date=+1d for tomorrow; start='Someday', start_date=None for someday). Also the same parametrize includes 'evening'/'tonight' without a has-auth-token skip guard - on a token-less machine those cases would fail rather than skip; add the guard.

title: update_todo/bulk paths: unknown primary id surfaces APPLESCRIPT_ERROR instead of NOT_FOUND - add a things.py pre-check or document
description: Found in hq-gbl.8 review: update_todo (scheduling/todo_operations.py ~1381-1397) has no things.py existence pre-check on the primary todo id - AppleScript 'to do id ...' fails and surfaces as APPLESCRIPT_ERROR with raw details, while CLAUDE.md's write-contract examples imply NOT_FOUND for missing targets (list_id/list_title moves DO return NOT_FOUND). Decide: add a read-only things.get pre-check returning NOT_FOUND (consistent, costs one read per update), or document APPLESCRIPT_ERROR as the contract for unknown primary ids. Check bulk_update_todos and delete_todo for consistency while there. Update tests/regression/test_update_todo.py's unknown-id assertion + CLAUDE.md accordingly.

title: Bug: checklist_items 100-item max documented but not enforced (101 items accepted)
description:
Found by hq-gbl.7 regression tests (strict xfail TestAddTodoChecklist::test_checklist_items_101_rejected_and_nothing_created in tests/regression/test_todo_create_delete.py). CLAUDE.md and tool docs state 'Maximum 100 checklist items per todo' but no code path (server.py, todo_operations.py, checklist tools) enforces any count limit before sending to the Things URL scheme - 101 items are accepted and created.
FIX: enforce the limit with a structured write error (e.g. VALIDATION_ERROR field=checklist_items, or a dedicated code) at the tool boundary for add_todo checklist_items AND add/prepend/replace_checklist_items (decide one code, document it); unit tests for 100 ok/101 rejected on all four tools; flip the strict xfail. title: Moving/adding under a completed heading or project silently reopens it; _check_heading_exists misses completed headings
description: Found during hq-f0w.28 live verification. (1) scheduling/todo_operations.py _check_heading_exists (~:408) queries things.tasks(type='heading', project=project_id) with things.py's default status='incomplete', so a completed heading triggers 'Heading ... was not found' even though the URL-scheme move succeeds. (2) More important: moving a to-do under a COMPLETED heading (or adding into a completed project) via URL scheme REOPENS that heading/project - a real data-altering side effect (confirmed live: project Agendas + headings Harold/Johan reopened). Fix: pass status=None to the heading lookup; when the matched heading (or the target project) is completed/canceled, do NOT silently proceed - either return a structured error (preferred: 'heading/project is completed; moving would reopen it') or require an explicit allow_reopen flag; same check in add_todo's heading/list resolution (_resolve_list_id can read things.get(project)['status']); tests with completed rows; CLAUDE.md warning; CHANGELOG. Also note in CLAUDE.md: things.py reads can lag ~1-2s after URL-scheme writes.
notes: Reviewer note: _check_heading_exists folded into _check_heading_status (tuple return) - symbol removed; edge: a to-do inside a completed project cannot be re-headed without reopening (documented).
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on 2nd review (1108 on base; 1166 after rebase). TARGET_COMPLETED guard on all add/update paths pre-write; status=None heading lookup; live: completed project stays completed.

title: AppleScript get_projects path: (area of theProject) as string errors, so area is always missing value; tag_names is a text property (comma-space)
description:
Discovered by the hq-f0w.8 reviewer (read-only probe against real Things 3). AppleScriptManager.get_projects currently has no callers in tools_helpers, so no user-visible impact today; fix before anything starts calling it (hq-nxu.8 may delete it instead - coordinate).

Done: contract xfails removed; real Things: AppleScriptManager.get_projects returns area ids and tag lists for a project with both.

title: URL-scheme post-create ID lookup can pick the wrong todo (duplicate titles) and returns success without an id on slow Things
description:
Write sweep S1. scheduling/todo_operations.py:290-312: after a things:///add, searches `to dos whose name is <title>` and takes the max creation date (1s granularity - ties with duplicate titles), after a fixed 0.5s sleep; on miss returns success:true with warning 'Todo ID not available' (:329).
Steps: 1. Snapshot the set of uuids with that title before the URL call (things.py or AppleScript), poll after with a deadline (e.g. up to 3s, 250ms steps) for a new uuid = after - before; if exactly one, return it; if several, return the newest with a warning; if none by the deadline, return success:false with a clear error (the URL may still have succeeded - say so). 2. Tests with mocked lookups for: immediate hit, delayed hit, duplicate titles, timeout. 3. Docs.
Done: live: two add_todo calls with the same title within a second return distinct correct uuids; suite green.
notes: Reviewer notes: each URL-scheme create now costs 2 title scans (~1.2-1.4s live vs 0.8s); _find_todo_ids_by_title returns [] on AppleScript failure for both snapshot and polls - a failed snapshot with a pre-existing same-title todo could return the wrong id (distinguish None vs [] in a follow-up); concurrent same-title creates both get newest id + warning (documented).
close_reason: Reviewer PASS (1193 on base; 1197 after rebase). Live: two same-title creates with quotes/backslash/comma -> distinct correct ids; trashed.

title: Tag names containing a comma are silently split; remove_tags bypasses tag policy and over-reports
description:
Write sweep C8/C9. All tag write sites join with ', '.join(tags) (todo_operations.py:99,545,679,824; write_operations.py:279,388); ParameterValidator.validate_tag_list passes ['home, office'] through, so Things receives 'home, office, urgent' -> three tags. write_operations.py:479-520 remove_tags never calls _prepare_tags (add_tags does at :414) and reports len(tags) requested rather than removed.
Steps: 1. validate_tag_list: reject tag names containing ',' with a structured error (Things itself cannot represent them via the comma-joined AppleScript API). 2. remove_tags: report removed = len(current) - len(remaining); decide whether policy validation applies to removal (likely no - removing an unknown tag is a no-op; document). 3. Tests. 4. Docs.
Done: suite green; live: remove_tags on a tag the todo lacks reports 0 removed.
notes: Reviewer notes: comma guard only in validate_tag_list (update_* list input); add_todo/add_project/add_area/add_tags with Python list input still pass comma names to the join (unreachable via MCP); remove_tags [] still rewrites unchanged tag string (no-op); CLAUDE.md tools list omits add_project/add_area.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on 2nd review (1193 on base; 1197 after rebase with test reconciliation vs hq-f0w.13 retrofits). Live: remove_tags mixed -> removed_count 1 / not_present.

title: when='evening'/'tonight' rejected; deadline relative-keyword acceptance differs between create and update
description:
Write sweep C6/C7. parameter_validator.py:709 validate_date_format(allow_relative=True) accepts only today/tomorrow/someday/anytime, so update_todo(when='evening') fails though Things supports Evening. server.py:465 validates deadline with allow_relative=False for add_todo while parameter_validator.py:713 (update path via write_operations.py:135) uses allow_relative=True, and locale_handler.normalize_date_input('today') then yields nothing so bulk_update_todos(deadline='today') silently skips (todo_operations.py:550).
Steps: 1. Add 'evening' (and 'tonight' as alias) to the relative allowlist and map to the correct AppleScript/URL semantics (Things: schedule today + evening flag; check how 'today' is implemented and whether AppleScript can set Evening - if only the URL scheme can (when=evening), route accordingly or document the limitation). 2. Make deadline validation consistent: either accept relative keywords end-to-end (resolve to a date before emitting) or reject them at both layers with the same error. 3. Tests enumerating all keywords for when and deadline on create/update/bulk. 4. Docs.
Done: update_todo(when='evening') works on real Things 3 (or returns a documented structured error if impossible); deadline='today' behaves identically on create/update/bulk; suite green.
notes: Mechanism: only the Things URL scheme sets This Evening (TMTask.startBucket 1); AppleScript schedule cannot. Reviewer follow-ups: whitespace-only when now silently no-op (hq-f0w.34); deadline rejection message wording; no-rollback on URL failure documented. Implementer copied the main-checkout .things-auth into the worktree for the live check and removed it (nothing leaked).
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on 2nd review (1218 on base; 1108 after rebase with tests-only reconciliation vs hq-f0w.13 meta-lint and hq-nxu.12 lookup shape). Live: update_todo(when='Tonight') / add_todo(when='tonight') -> startBucket=1; trashed.

title: update_* cannot clear a field: notes='' / deadline='' are treated as absent; sanitize_string('') returns None
description:
