title: GH#9 item 3d: update_todo(heading=...) to move an existing to-do under a heading (URL-scheme update)
description:
Input: GH #9 asks to 'place tasks under the correct heading'. Creation is handled by hq-f0w.5; this bead covers existing to-dos. Things URL scheme `update` accepts `heading` / `heading-id` (moves the to-do under that heading in its project) and REQUIRES the auth token (things:///update?auth-token=...). AppleScript cannot do this. Note: MoveOperations.move_to_project(..., heading=...) exists (services/move_operations.py:211-227, builds 'project:ID:heading') but is dead code and the destination parser (:274, :385) would mis-parse it - do NOT route through it; leave that code untouched (file a follow-up bead if you think it should be removed).

Steps:
1. Add `heading: Optional[str] = None` to the update_todo MCP tool (server.py ~:448-457) and thread it into scheduling/todo_operations.py update_todo.
2. In update_todo: when heading is set, after the AppleScript updates (or instead, if the only change is heading) issue a things:///update URL with id=<todo id>, heading=<title>, auth-token from the existing auth-token mechanism (look for how the URL-scheme update/auth token is loaded - e.g. .things-auth file / THINGS_AUTH_TOKEN - and reuse it). If no auth token is configured, return {"success": False, "error": "..."} naming the env var/file needed, without partially applying other fields (do the auth check BEFORE any AppleScript write). Optionally also accept `heading` moving the todo into a different project when list_id is also given (URL update supports list-id + heading together) - if you implement this, test it; if not, document that heading applies within the todo's current project.
3. Unit tests: update_todo(heading=...) emits a things:///update URL with id+heading+auth-token (mock the executor); missing auth token -> structured error and no AppleScript call; heading combined with title/notes still applies the AppleScript fields.
4. Docs: CLAUDE.md + README update_todo docs (auth token requirement, heading must exist in the project); `python scripts/gen_manifest_tools.py --check` (signature change) - --write if drift.
5. `pytest tests/unit -q` green.

Done criteria: real Things 3 check - on a throwaway to-do in a project that has headings (see hq-f0w.5 for setup), update_todo(id, heading=<title>) then things.get(uuid)['heading_title'] == <title>; then trash it; unit suite green.

Edge cases: heading title needing percent-encoding; todo not in a project (URL scheme will ignore - surface a warning if things.get(uuid)['project'] is None); auth token present but wrong (Things shows an error dialog, URL call returns - document that no programmatic error is available).
notes: Reviewer minor: _check_heading_exists warning text says 'Things will still create the to-do' when used from update_todo (cosmetic); list_id tool description still says 'Project/area ID' though area targets only warn.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS on 2nd review (1131 on base). Live: no-token structured error path verified; URL contents verified with mocked innermost executor; authenticated round-trip deferred to hq-f0w.28 (no token on this machine).

title: GH#9 item 3c: new get_project_headings tool (read heading structure of a project)
description:
Input: GH #9 item 3 asks for a way to read heading structure within a project. things.py supports things.tasks(type='heading', project=<uuid>) (verified: 30 headings on the dev DB) and to-dos carry heading/heading_title (exposed by the sibling bead hq-f0w.4). No tool exposes headings today; nearest workaround is search_advanced(type='heading') which returns headings but not their member counts.

Steps:
1. Add a read operation in tools_helpers/read_operations.py: get_project_headings(project_id) -> list of {"uuid", "title", "index" (things.py order), "todoCount" (open to-dos under that heading via things.todos(heading=uuid)) } preserving Things' heading order; return a structured error if the project_id does not resolve (things.get returns None or type != 'project').
2. Register an MCP tool `get_project_headings(project_id: str, mode: str = 'auto')` in server.py using the same _read_result / structured_content shape as other list tools ({items,count,total,mode,limit,offset}); follow the existing async wrapper pattern. Docstring must state: headings cannot be created/renamed/deleted via the public Things 3 APIs (no AppleScript heading class; URL scheme only places to-dos under existing headings or seeds headings at project creation via add-project `##` lines) - this tool is read-only by design.
3. Run `python scripts/gen_manifest_tools.py --write` so manifest.json lists the new tool; the guard test tests/unit/test_manifest_tools_sync.py must pass. Check get_server_capabilities tool-count logic still works (computed at runtime - no edit needed, but verify).
4. Unit tests: mocked things.tasks/things.todos -> correct items, ordering, todoCount, error on unknown project, structured_content shape.
5. Docs: CLAUDE.md (Hierarchical Organization section) + README tool list: document get_project_headings and the create/update/delete limitation; advertise the tool so the AI knows it exists.
6. `pytest tests/unit -q` green.

Done criteria: real Things 3 check - call the sync helper on a project that has headings and confirm titles/order/todoCount match things.py; manifest in sync; unit suite green.

Edge cases: project with zero headings -> empty items, count 0; heading with zero to-dos -> todoCount 0; project_id that is actually an area or to-do -> structured error.
notes: Reviewer follow-ups: empty-result envelope reports mode 'auto' (context_manager empty path never resolves AUTO; pre-existing, epic-wide - CLAUDE.md overstates 'never auto'); summary mode has no preview for this method; error shape differs - hq-f0w.19.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS in run 2 (1131 passed). Tool-specific field filtering; global sets unchanged. Live: 3 headings with todoCount 2/1/1 on Complete Weekly Review; zero-heading project -> [].

title: Audit pre-handshake boot path for blocking work; file follow-up beads
description: INPUT: everything executed before FastMCP serves the stdio handshake: src/things_mcp/__main__.py, main.py, server.py __init__/_configure_logging/_register_tools, services/applescript_manager.py __init__/_load_auth_token, tools.py ThingsTools.__init__ and every constructor it calls (PureAppleScriptScheduler, ValidationService, MoveOperationsTools, TagValidationService, ReadOperations, WriteOperations, BulkOperations, ResponseOptimizer, ContextAwareResponseManager, operation_queue, shared_cache), plus module-level statements in all imported things_mcp modules. WORK: enumerate every subprocess call, network call, file write, lock acquisition, or unbounded file read reachable during boot; check _configure_logging for file-handler paths that could block (e.g., log file on slow/locked volume); check for module-level osascript or 'import things' style side effects. Known-clean already (do not re-litigate, just confirm): lazy Things probe per main.py:53-59, _load_auth_token file-only reads. OUTPUT: findings written into this bead's notes as a table (call site -> blocking potential -> verdict), and one new bd task filed under epic hq-l1a per confirmed blocking call with a concrete fix. DONE-CRITERIA: notes contain the audit table covering every listed module; zero or more follow-up beads filed and linked; no code changes in this task.
notes:
## Pre-handshake boot path audit (hq-l1a.3)

| Call site (file:line) | Boot phase | Blocking potential | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `__main__.py:5-6` boot_marker/arm_boot_watchdog | process-start | stdlib only (time, os, sys, faulthandler) | CLEAN |
| `__main__.py:8` `from .main import main` | process-start -> import cascade | triggers transitive import of server.py -> tools.py -> `import things` (see below) | SUSPECT (carrier of the real issue) |
| `main.py:11-13` module imports (boot_trace, server, applescript_manager) | import cascade | same cascade as above | SUSPECT (carrier) |
| `main.py:21-25` `ServerManager.__init__` / `_setup_signal_handlers` | pre-config | `signal.signal()` only | CLEAN |
| `server.py:12-17` `from dotenv import load_dotenv; load_dotenv()` (module level) | import cascade | walks parent dirs from CWD looking for `.env` (bounded stat calls); could be slow if CWD is on a deep/slow/networked path, but bounded and typically sub-ms | CLEAN (low-risk) |
| `server.py:19` `from fastmcp import FastMCP` | import cascade | pulls in pydantic/uvicorn/httpx/mcp-sdk transitively; pure interpreter+import cost, no explicit I/O in our code, but cold-disk/cold-page-cache import of a large dependency tree can genuinely take seconds on an overnight-cold machine | CLEAN (code) / plausible EXTERNAL cause |
| `server.py:25` `from .tools import ThingsTools` -> `tools.py:7` `import things` -> `things/database.py:31-34` module-level `next(glob.iglob(os.path.expanduser(DEFAULT_FILEPATH_31616502)))` | import cascade (before any boot_marker fires except watchdog-armed) | **Unconditional, synchronous, unbounded filesystem glob** over `~/Library/Group Containers/JLMPQHK86H.com.culturedcode.ThingsMac/ThingsData-*/...` executed once at import time, on the same thread that must complete before `ThingsMCPServer.__init__` even starts. No timeout, no boot_marker bracketing it, not skippable via `THINGSDB` env var (that only affects `Database.__init__`, not this module-level constant). If `~/Library` is on a slow/locked/networked volume at cold overnight boot (external drive not yet mounted, FileVault unlock delay, Spotlight/mds or backup lock contention on Group Containers), this glob can stall indefinitely with zero stderr output — matches the reported symptom exactly. | **CONFIRMED-BLOCKING** |
| `services/applescript_manager.py:39-70` `AppleScriptManager.__init__` (incl. `_load_auth_token`, `AppleScriptExecutor()`, `AppleScriptFormatters()`, `AppleScriptQueries()`, `AppleScriptParser()`) | applescript-manager-ready | `_load_auth_token` is file-only reads of 3 candidate paths (KNOWN-CLEAN per brief); the 4 sub-constructors just set attributes, no I/O, no subprocess | CLEAN |
| `services/applescript/executor.py:24` `AppleScriptExecutor.__init__` | applescript-manager-ready | attribute assignment only; class-level `asyncio.Lock()` created at import (safe under Python 3.10+, no loop binding at creation) | CLEAN |
| `services/applescript/parser.py:62` `AppleScriptParser.__init__` | applescript-manager-ready | calls `reset()`, pure in-memory state | CLEAN |
| `services/applescript/formatters.py`, `queries.py` | applescript-manager-ready | no `__init__`, static/stateless methods | CLEAN |
| `tools.py:32` `ThingsTools.__init__` -> `PureAppleScriptScheduler`, `ValidationService`, `MoveOperationsTools`, `ResponseOptimizer`, `TagValidationService`, `ReadOperations`, `WriteOperations`, `BulkOperations` | tools-registered (pre) | all constructors (`pure_applescript_scheduler.py:42`, `services/validation_service.py:20`, `move_operations.py:22`, `response_optimizer.py:25`, `services/tag_service.py:32`, `tools_helpers/read_operations.py:20`, `tools_helpers/write_operations.py:20`, `tools_helpers/bulk_operations.py:20`) only store references/config; no subprocess, network, file I/O, or locks at construction | CLEAN |
| `tools_helpers/read_operations.py:8` `import things` (redundant transitive import, already loaded via tools.py) | import cascade | same module-level glob as above, already executed once (Python import cache) — no additional cost, but confirms the dependency is unconditional in two places | CLEAN (no additional cost; same root cause as above) |
| `context_manager.py:396` `ContextAwareResponseManager.__init__` (+ `SmartDefaultManager`, `ProgressiveDisclosureEngine`, `ResponseSizeEstimator`) | tools-registered (pre) | pure in-memory data structures | CLEAN |
| `server.py:96-132` `_configure_logging()` | logging-configured | Console `StreamHandler` used by default (`config.log_file_path is None`). **If** `THINGS_MCP_LOG_FILE_PATH` is set, does `Path.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)` then `logging.FileHandler(path)` (blocking `open()`), with no timeout — could stall on a slow/locked/networked log directory (e.g. external volume asleep, log rotation holding a lock at 01:00). Confirmed via the actual deployed Claude Desktop config (`~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json`) that `THINGS_MCP_LOG_FILE_PATH` is **not** set for this server today, so this path is currently inactive/unreached | CLEAN (as currently deployed) / SUSPECT (latent, only if ever configured) |
| `server.py:167` `_register_tools()` | tools-registered | Only defines/decorates async closures with `@self.mcp.tool()`; no tool body executes at registration time | CLEAN |
| `server.py:134-165` `_register_shutdown_handlers()` | tools-registered (post) | `atexit.register`, `signal.signal` only | CLEAN |
| `operation_queue.py` (`get_operation_queue`/global `_global_queue`) | not on boot path | Only instantiated lazily on first tool call (`queue_status`, bulk ops); never touched during `__init__` chain | CLEAN / not reachable at boot |
| `shared_cache.py` (fcntl locks, file I/O, `threading.RLock`) | not on boot path | grep confirms this module is never imported anywhere else in `things_mcp` — dead code, unreachable | CLEAN / not reachable |
| `locale_aware_dates.py:484` module-level `locale_handler = LocaleAwareDateHandler()` | import cascade | `__init__` only logs; no `locale.setlocale()` or I/O | CLEAN |
| `config.py` `load_config_from_env` -> `ThingsMCPConfig.from_env_file` | config-loaded | `Path(".env").exists()` stat (cheap) when no env_file given; pydantic `BaseSettings` reads `os.environ` only | CLEAN |
| main.py:53-59 lazy Things probe comment | n/a | confirmed absent from startup path as documented | CLEAN (confirmed, not re-litigated) |
| `services/applescript_manager.py:72-95` `_load_auth_token` | applescript-manager-ready | file-only reads of 3 fixed candidate paths | CLEAN (confirmed, not re-litigated) |

### Verdict counts
CLEAN: 20 · SUSPECT: 3 (import cascade carriers / latent file-logging path / cold fastmcp import) · CONFIRMED-BLOCKING: 1

### Conclusion (ranked hypotheses)
1. **Most plausible: the `things` library's module-level `glob.iglob()` over `~/Library/Group Containers/JLMPQHK86H.com.culturedcode.ThingsMac/ThingsData-*/...`**, executed unconditionally and synchronously the moment `import things` runs (transitively pulled in via `server.py -> tools.py`, before any of our own code executes and before most boot_markers fire). It has no timeout, cannot be bypassed via `THINGSDB` env var (that only affects `Database.__init__`, not this constant), and touches a filesystem location that plausibly stalls at overnight cold-start (external/synced volume asleep, FileVault unlock latency, Spotlight/mds or Time Machine local-snapshot contention on Group Containers around 01:00). This is a real, unbounded, blocking filesystem call reachable on every single boot, in third-party code we cannot edit in place but can shield ourselves from.
2. **Second: cold interpreter/import stall**, i.e. the sheer cost of importing `fastmcp` and its dependency tree (pydantic, httpx, uvicorn, mcp-sdk, etc.) on a machine where the page cache and/or disk have gone cold overnight (spun-down disk, first access after sleep, antivirus/Spotlight scanning newly-touched files). This is external to our code (no bug to fix) but is a legitimate contributor to intermittent multi-second-to-minute cold-start variance, and is indistinguishable from cause #1 without the boot markers/watchdog stack dump already added on this branch — which is exactly the right next diagnostic (a real overnight hang capture will show whether the watchdog fires during `import` before any marker, pointing at #1, or while genuinely inside `FastMCP`/`mcp.run()`, pointing elsewhere).
3. Third (much less likely given current deployment): the file-logging path in `_configure_logging()` is a real, unguarded blocking `open()` on a configurable path, but confirmed inactive in the actual deployed Claude Desktop config for this server today, so it cannot be the cause of the *currently observed* hangs — only a latent risk if a log file path is ever configured on a slow/networked volume.

No sqlite/db connections, subprocess/osascript spawns, or network calls were found anywhere on the boot path itself (the actual `sqlite3.connect()` inside `things.database.Database.__init__` and all `osascript` subprocess calls are correctly deferred to first tool invocation, matching the documented lazy-probe design).

title: doctor: check_environment's bare 'import things' can hang behind a stalled bounded import
description: Reviewer note on hq-dzy.3: doctor.py check_environment does a bare 'import things' for the version probe. If the DB check's daemon thread is stalled inside the unbounded things import (the exact TCC/glob failure doctor diagnoses), the env check then blocks on Python's import lock with no timeout, hanging doctor on the machines it's meant to help. Fix: check sys.modules first and report 'unknown (import pending)' instead of importing, or reuse things_import's bounded import. Also consider: DB-check timeout currently maps to WARN — decide if a hang should be FAIL. Add a unit test with a fake stuck import.
acceptance_criteria: doctor never blocks on import locks; env row degrades gracefully; test covers it.
close_reason: Reviewer PASS; committed on epic/hq-dzy
